# pylopdf

> Edit, render, extract, and create PDFs in Python. pylopdf aims to do
> everything pymupdf can do with PDF files through an API of its own, is
> built on the Rust PDF engines lopdf, hayro, and krilla, and is MIT licensed.

Documentation: https://pylopdf.haya.works/
Japanese documentation: https://pylopdf.haya.works/ja/
Simplified Chinese documentation: https://pylopdf.haya.works/zh-cn/
Korean documentation: https://pylopdf.haya.works/ko/
Source: https://github.com/yhay81/pylopdf
PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pylopdf/

Pages:
- Getting started: https://pylopdf.haya.works/getting-started/
- Migrating from pymupdf: https://pylopdf.haya.works/migration/
- Offline OCR: https://pylopdf.haya.works/ocr/
- Concurrency: https://pylopdf.haya.works/concurrency/
- WebAssembly: https://pylopdf.haya.works/wasm/
- Ecosystem recipes: https://pylopdf.haya.works/ecosystem/
- API reference: https://pylopdf.haya.works/api/
- Security: https://pylopdf.haya.works/security/
- API stability: https://pylopdf.haya.works/stability/
- Benchmarks: https://pylopdf.haya.works/benchmarks/
- Contributing and support: https://pylopdf.haya.works/contributing/

Key facts:
- MIT licensed, no required Python dependencies, Python 3.11 or newer.
- Wheels for Linux, macOS, and Windows, including free-threaded CPython 3.14t
  and 3.15t, plus a WebAssembly wheel for Pyodide 0.28.3 and Cloudflare
  Python Workers.
- Pre-1.0: the next release redesigns the API (ROADMAP.md and
  api/DESIGN.md in the repository); the documentation follows the main
  branch.
- PDF files only. Typesetting, digital signatures, and PDF/A validation are
  done with typst, pyHanko, and veraPDF.
- Page numbers start at 0 everywhere; get_outline/set_outline replace
  pymupdf's 1-based get_toc/set_toc.
- Coordinates are points with a top-left origin in the displayed page,
  shared by extraction, search, drawing, and rendering.
- Point, Matrix, Rect, IRect, and Quad are immutable NamedTuples with
  pymupdf's operators: p * m, left * right (left transform first), ~m,
  r | p (include), r & o (intersect), r * m (transform), p in r. Replace
  in-place methods such as transform, normalize, or pretranslate with
  assignment of the operator result (r = r.normalized()).
- page.content() returns every text run, path, and image a page paints, in
  paint order, as immutable values with glyph outline boxes, paints, strokes,
  and the clips, transparency groups, and marked content around each item.
- get_pixmap(matrix=) takes scaling matrices only; dpi= takes precedence.
- DocumentLimits.web() and LimitError.code bound untrusted input.

Migrating pymupdf code:
- python -m pylopdf.migrate PATH (pip install "pylopdf[migrate]") renames the
  fitz and pymupdf imports, rewrites mechanical replacements such as
  get_toc/set_toc, embfile_*, xref_* readers and in-place geometry methods,
  and adds a "# TODO(pylopdf): <hint>" comment above every statement that
  still needs a person; it then lists those steps as path:line: message.
- Looking up a pymupdf name that pylopdf lacks raises AttributeError whose
  message names the replacement or the milestone that plans it.

pymupdf name map (generated from api/pymupdf-parity.json; each pymupdf name that pylopdf replaced, its
replacement, and the migration hint):
- DisplayList -> Content: Use the Content that page.content() returns; it records the page's items once and can be read any number of times.
- DisplayList.rect -> Page.rect: Read page.rect, the display area in which the content items are positioned.
- Document.copy_page -> Document.fullcopy_page: pylopdf never shares page objects; use fullcopy_page.
- Document.embfile_add -> Document.attachments: Use doc.attachments.add(name, data, filename=..., description=...).
- Document.embfile_count -> Document.attachments: Use len(doc.attachments).
- Document.embfile_del -> Document.attachments: Use del doc.attachments[name].
- Document.embfile_get -> Document.attachments: Use doc.attachments[name].read().
- Document.embfile_info -> Document.attachments: Read name, filename, description, size, creation_date, and mod_date from doc.attachments[name].
- Document.embfile_names -> Document.attachments: Use list(doc.attachments).
- Document.embfile_upd -> Document.attachments: Use doc.attachments[name].write(data).
- Document.get_new_xref -> Objects.add: Call doc.objects.add(value), which creates the object and returns its object number.
- Document.get_toc -> Document.get_outline: pylopdf's get_outline uses zero-based pages; get_toc used one-based pages.
- Document.is_stream -> Stream: Check isinstance(doc.objects[xref], pylopdf.Stream).
- Document.language -> Document.language_tag: pylopdf's language_tag keeps the complete BCP 47 tag, such as zh-TW, where pymupdf's language keeps at most three letters.
- Document.pdf_catalog -> Document.catalog: Use doc.catalog, a live dictionary handle; doc.catalog.xref is its object number.
- Document.pdf_trailer -> Document.trailer: Use doc.trailer, a live dictionary handle, instead of its PDF syntax.
- Document.set_language -> Document.set_language_tag: pylopdf's set_language_tag writes the complete BCP 47 tag, such as zh-TW, where pymupdf's set_language keeps at most three letters.
- Document.set_toc -> Document.set_outline: pylopdf's set_outline uses zero-based pages; set_toc used one-based pages.
- Document.to_text -> Document.get_text: Call Document.get_text() for the plain text of every page.
- Document.update_object -> Document.objects: Assign a typed value to doc.objects[xref] instead of PDF syntax.
- Document.update_stream -> Stream.write: Call doc.objects[xref].write(data), which Flate-compresses unless filter=None.
- Document.xref_copy -> Document.objects: Assign doc.objects[source] to doc.objects[target], which copies the object.
- Document.xref_get_key -> Dictionary: Use doc.objects[xref].get(key), which returns a typed value instead of a (type, syntax) pair.
- Document.xref_get_keys -> Dictionary: Use list(doc.objects[xref]), whose keys carry no leading slash.
- Document.xref_is_font -> Dictionary: Check doc.objects[xref].get('Type') == 'Font'.
- Document.xref_is_image -> Dictionary: Check doc.objects[xref].get('Subtype') == 'Image'.
- Document.xref_is_stream -> Stream: Check isinstance(doc.objects[xref], pylopdf.Stream).
- Document.xref_is_xobject -> Dictionary: Check doc.objects[xref].get('Type') == 'XObject'.
- Document.xref_length -> Document.objects: Use max(doc.objects) + 1; len(doc.objects) counts the object numbers in use.
- Document.xref_object -> Document.objects: Use doc.objects[xref], a typed value or handle, instead of its PDF syntax.
- Document.xref_set_key -> Dictionary: Assign doc.objects[xref][key] = value with a typed value, such as pylopdf.Name('Page') for a name.
- Document.xref_stream -> Stream.read: Use doc.objects[xref].read().
- Document.xref_stream_raw -> Stream.read: Use doc.objects[xref].read(decode=False).
- Document.xref_xml_metadata -> Document.catalog: Use doc.catalog.get('Metadata'), a Stream whose xref is the metadata object number.
- DocumentWriter -> Builder: Call pylopdf.create(), draw each page in a `with builder.page(size) as canvas:` block, and write the document with builder.to_bytes() or builder.finish().
- DocumentWriter.__enter__ -> Builder.page: Draw each page in a `with builder.page(size) as canvas:` block; the block adds the page when it ends.
- DocumentWriter.__exit__ -> Builder.to_bytes: Write the document with builder.to_bytes(), or open it with builder.finish().
- DocumentWriter.begin_page -> Builder.page: Use `with builder.page(size) as canvas:`; the canvas draws the page and the block adds it.
- DocumentWriter.close -> Builder.to_bytes: Write the document with builder.to_bytes(), or open it with builder.finish().
- DocumentWriter.end_page -> Builder.page: The `with builder.page(size) as canvas:` block adds the page when it ends.
- FileNotFoundError -> FileNotFoundError: Catch Python's built-in FileNotFoundError, which pylopdf raises for a missing file.
- IRect.__setitem__ -> IRect: IRect values are immutable; build a new IRect instead.
- IRect.include_point -> IRect.__or__: Use r | p, which returns a new IRect.
- IRect.include_rect -> IRect.__or__: Use r | other, which returns a new IRect.
- IRect.intersect -> IRect.__and__: Use r & other, which returns a new IRect.
- IRect.normalize -> IRect.normalized: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new IRect.
- IRect.transform -> IRect.__mul__: Use r * m, which returns a new IRect.
- Matrix.__setitem__ -> Matrix: Matrix values are immutable; build a new Matrix instead.
- Matrix.concat -> Matrix.__mul__: Use one * two, which returns a new Matrix.
- Matrix.invert -> Matrix.__invert__: Use ~m, which returns the inverse.
- Matrix.prerotate -> Matrix.__mul__: Use pylopdf.Matrix(deg) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
- Matrix.prescale -> Matrix.__mul__: Use pylopdf.Matrix(sx, sy) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
- Matrix.preshear -> Matrix.__mul__: Use pylopdf.Matrix(h, v, 1) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
- Matrix.pretranslate -> Matrix.__mul__: Use pylopdf.Matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, tx, ty) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
- Page.get_bboxlog -> Page.content: Call page.content(); every item has a bbox and a kind, and its context lists the clips around it.
- Page.get_cdrawings -> Page.content: Read page.content().paths, whose segments, paints, and strokes are immutable values.
- Page.get_displaylist -> Page.content: Call page.content(), which returns the page's painted items as an immutable Content sequence.
- Page.get_image_bbox -> Page.content: Keep the items of page.content().images whose xref is the image's object number, and read their bbox and matrix.
- Page.get_image_rects -> Page.content: Keep the items of page.content().images whose xref is the image's object number, and read their bbox and matrix.
- Page.get_texttrace -> Page.content: Call page.content() and read the glyphs of its text_runs, each run with its font, size, paints, and graphics context.
- Page.last_point -> PathBuilder.current_point: Build the path with a PathBuilder and read its current_point, the end of its last segment.
- Page.run -> Page.content: Call page.content() for the items that the page paints; pylopdf has no device protocol.
- Point.__setitem__ -> Point: Point values are immutable; build a new Point instead.
- Point.transform -> Point.__mul__: Use p * m, which returns a new Point.
- Quad.__setitem__ -> Quad: Quad values are immutable; build a new Quad instead.
- Quad.transform -> Quad.__mul__: Use q * m, which returns a new Quad.
- Rect.__setitem__ -> Rect: Rect values are immutable; build a new Rect instead.
- Rect.include_point -> Rect.__or__: Use r | p, which returns a new Rect.
- Rect.include_rect -> Rect.__or__: Use r | other, which returns a new Rect.
- Rect.intersect -> Rect.__and__: Use r & other, which returns a new Rect.
- Rect.normalize -> Rect.normalized: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new Rect.
- Rect.transform -> Rect.__mul__: Use r * m, which returns a new Rect.
- get_pdf_str -> String: Write a Python str into the object model, which encodes it as a PDF text string, or read String.text.
- set_log -> PylopdfWarning: Filter or record pylopdf's diagnostics as PylopdfWarning with the warnings module.
- set_messages -> PylopdfWarning: Filter or record pylopdf's diagnostics as PylopdfWarning with the warnings module.
